extra.message: The route handler passes attacker-controlled req.query.name directly to eval(). A request such as GET /api/v2/user?name=require('child_process').execSync('id') results in arbitrary server-side code execution (RCE). The route is also unauthenticated.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')

extra.message: The /contact route reads the user-controlled query.url parameter and passes it to needle.get(), causing the server to issue an HTTP request to an arbitrary attacker-specified URL. This enables Server-Side Request Forgery against internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: After fetching query.url, the handler redirects the client to the same user-supplied URL with res.redirect(query.url). This allows an attacker to craft a link such as /contact?url=https://evil.example that redirects victims to an arbitrary external site (phishing / credential theft).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The JWT signing key is hardcoded as the literal string 'hardsecret' in jwt.verify(). Because the secret is in source control and guessable, an attacker can forge valid auth tokens for arbitrary user IDs, resulting in authentication bypass.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: Auth tokens are signed with the hardcoded secret 'hardsecret' in generateAuthToken(). A hardcoded, predictable signing key lets an attacker mint their own valid JWTs and impersonate any user.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: GET /api/v1/tasks has no auth middleware and calls Task.find({}), returning every task belonging to every user to any unauthenticated caller. This is a broken access control / sensitive data exposure issue.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: GET /api/v1/users/:name is unauthenticated and looks up any user by name, returning their profile data. This allows anonymous user enumeration and disclosure of account details.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: PATCH /api/v1/users/:id authenticates the caller but then loads the target with User.findById(req.params.id) without verifying it matches req.user._id. Any authenticated user can modify another user's name, email, and password (including taking over the account).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: DELETE /api/v1/users/:id authenticates the caller but deletes the user identified solely by req.params.id via User.findByIdAndDelete(), with no check that the id belongs to the caller. Any authenticated user can delete arbitrary accounts.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: PATCH /api/v1/tasks/:id loads the task with Task.findById(req.params.id) and then updates it, without scoping the query to owner: req.user._id. Any authenticated user can modify tasks belonging to other users (IDOR).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: findByCredentials builds the query as User.findOne({ email }) using the raw req.body.email value (see /dashboard handler). Because express.json() parses objects, an attacker can send {"email":{"$ne":null}} and inject MongoDB operators into the query, enabling NoSQL injection / user enumeration.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: updatePageDom assigns a template string containing todo.description directly to newListItem.innerHTML. Task descriptions come from the server and are never sanitized server-side, so a stored XSS payload such as executes when the task list is rendered.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The display() helper injects the server-returned userData value into innerHTML without escaping. A user-controlled profile field (name/email) containing HTML/JavaScript is rendered as markup, leading to DOM-based XSS.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The profile page sets document.querySelector('#email').innerHTML from data.user.email returned by /api/v2/profile. Email is attacker-controlled at registration and is not HTML-escaped, so it can inject script/markup (DOM XSS).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The AJAX success handler writes the server response msg.msg into the DOM using jQuery's .html(), which interprets its argument as HTML. If the response body is influenced by user input, this results in DOM-based XSS.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The inline script reads the 'name' query parameter via getQueryParameter() and concatenates it into an HTML string assigned to resultsEl.innerHTML (line 190). A crafted URL such as /contact.html?name= executes arbitrary script in the victim's browser.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The authentication JWT is set with res.cookie('auth_token', token) without HttpOnly or Secure flags. The token is therefore readable by client-side JavaScript, so any XSS can steal the session token, and it can be transmitted over plain HTTP.

cwe: CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The login handler sets the authentication JWT via res.cookie('auth_token', token) without HttpOnly or Secure flags, exposing the session token to client-side script access and interception over HTTP.
